q: ____ is primarily used in the production of stainless steel. (2024)
e: Nickel is widely added to steel to form stainless steel alloys that offer enhanced resistance to corrosion.

q: ____ ion has brilliant blue colour used as paint, ink, and pigments. (2025)
e: Cobalt compounds produce vibrant blue pigments widely used in inks, paints, and ceramics.

q: Iron and ____ are essential metals used in modern medicine. (2025)
e: Both iron and copper play critical metabolic roles in the human body and in medical applications.

q: ____ is used for roofs-flooring and ceiling decoration in buildings. (2024)
e: Titanium is durable and corrosion-resistant, making it ideal for decorative and structural building panels.

q: In general, the ions of transition elements have an electronic configuration of ____. (2024)
e: Transition metal ions typically retain a valence d-orbital electron structure represented as (n-1) d¹⁻¹⁰.

q: Transition elements exhibit ____ oxidation states. (2025)
e: Because total valence electrons reside in both 4s and 3d subshells, transition metals exhibit variable oxidation states.

q: One cubic centimeter (1 cm³) cube of iron is ____ times heavier than a 1 cm³ cube of sodium. (2025)
e: Iron has a density of roughly 7.87 g/cm³, which makes it approximately 8 times heavier than sodium.

q: Cobalt ion has brilliant ____ colour used as paint, ink, and pigments. (2024)
e: Cobalt ions impart a distinctive blue color used in pigments.

q: Titanium(IV) chloride is used for the manufacturing of high density ____ in industries. (2025)
e: Titanium(IV) chloride serves as a catalyst component in the industrial polymerization of high-density polyethene.

q: In general, the ions of transition elements have an electronic configuration of ____. (2025)
e: Transition element cations retain partially filled d-orbitals with configuration (n-1) d¹⁻¹⁰.

q: Tobacco smoking is a significant source of ____ exposure. (2025)
e: Tobacco plants absorb cadmium from the soil, making cigarette smoke a major exposure source.

q: The transition elements have a ____ density. (2025)
e: Metallic bonding and small atomic radii give 3d transition metals relatively high densities.

q: ____ is a good conductor of electricity and it is used for electrical wire, circuit boards, water pipes, and industrial machinery. (2025)
e: Copper exhibits high electrical conductivity and corrosion resistance, making it suitable for electrical wiring.

q: The argon core shortened electronic configuration of ₂₁Sc represents ____. (2025)
e: Scandium has 21 electrons, giving it the abbreviated electron configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d¹.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an ____ called steel. (2025)
e: Mixing iron with carbon creates steel, which is an alloy with higher tensile strength.

q: ____ steel is extremely strong and is used for railway tracks. (2025)
e: Manganese steel possesses high impact strength and resistance to wear, ideal for railway lines.

q: In the transition elements, the ____ orbital is the outermost orbital. (2025)
e: For 3d transition series elements, the 4s subshell is the principal energy level outermost orbital.

q: ____ is an integral part of modern construction because it is highly corrosion-resistant. (2025)
e: Titanium forms a protective oxide layer that resists corrosion, benefiting long-term construction.

q: The first ionization energies (IE) of scandium to copper ____ only slightly as the positive charge on the nucleus increases. (2025)
e: First ionization energies increase across the series due to nuclear charge increase compensated by d-electron shielding.

q: Copper is considered a transition element because the Cu²⁺ ion has ____ 3d orbital. (2025)
e: The Cu²⁺ ion has a 3d⁹ electron configuration, leaving an incomplete d-subshell.

q: Iron combined with non-metal carbon produces an alloy called ____. (2025)
e: Carbon combined with iron yields steel alloys.

q: The 3d transition elements are silvery-white except for ____ which is brownish-red in colour. (2025)
e: Unlike other 3d series metals, copper displays a characteristic brownish-red metallic luster.

q: Copper has been used to treat ____ disease and Menkes disease. (2025)
e: Copper imbalance diseases include Wilson's disease and Menkes disease.

q: One cubic centimetre cube of iron is ____ times heavier than a 1 cm³ cube of soidum. (2025)
e: Iron is approximately eight times denser than sodium.

q: Most transition elements can form ____ ions. (2025)
e: Available d-orbitals and high ionic charge densities allow transition metals to readily form complex ions.

q: Iron, cobalt, and ____ are ferromagnetic substances. (2026)
e: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are the classic elements displaying ferromagnetism at room temperature.

q: All the transition elements in 3d series have quite similar radii, which accounts for their ability to blend together to form ____. (2026)
e: Similar metallic radii allow atoms of 3d metals to readily substitute each other in solid solution alloys.

q: Vanadium is used to form alloys of steel with ____. (2026)
e: Vanadium-steel alloys are formed by combining vanadium with iron to increase strength and fatigue resistance.
